hints.title: Iterative String Copy Bottleneck Obstacle
hints.text: Iterative search-and-delete loops cause repeated string copying and quadratic runtime. How can checking each character against the tail of a growing output sequence collapse adjacent case-inverted pairs in linear time?

hints.title: ASCII Difference 32 Invariant
hints.text: Two characters form an invalid adjacent pair if and only if abs(ord(c1) - ord(c2)) == 32. Cancelling them causes their respective left and right neighbors to touch.

hints.title: Tail Comparison Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an empty list. For each character ch in s: if the list is non-empty and abs(ord(list[-1]) - ord(ch)) == 32, pop the last element; otherwise append ch. Return the joined list.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 100)
complexity.notes: Single pass where each character is pushed and popped at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Repeatedly searching for case-inverted pairs and slicing strings runs in O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tail comparison on an auxiliary list reduces execution to strictly O(N) operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing the ASCII difference of 32 between uppercase and lowercase letters.
